an4.191:1.1: “Monks, when the teachings have been followed by ear, recited by speech, examined by mind, and well penetrated by view, four rewards can be expected.
an4.191:1.3: “There is the case where a monk has mastered the Dhamma:
an4.191:1.4: dialogues, narratives of mixed prose & verse, explanations, verses, spontaneous exclamations, quotations, birth stories, amazing events, question & answer sessions [the earliest classifications of the Buddha’s teachings].
an4.191:1.5: In him, these teachings have been followed by ear, recited by speech, examined by mind, and well penetrated by view.
an4.191:1.6: Passing away when his mindfulness is muddled, he arises in a certain group of devas.
an4.191:1.7: To him, happy there, they recite verses of Dhamma.
an4.191:1.8: Slow is the arising of his mindfulness,
an4.191:1.9: but when mindful, he quickly arrives at distinction.
an4.191:1.10: When the teachings have been followed by ear, recited by speech, examined by mind, and well penetrated by view, this is the first reward that can be expected.
an4.191:2.1: “Further, there is the case where a monk has mastered the Dhamma:
an4.191:2.3: In him, these teachings have been followed by ear, recited by speech, examined by mind, and well penetrated by view.
an4.191:2.4: Passing away when his mindfulness is muddled, he arises in a certain group of devas.
an4.191:2.5: It doesn’t happen that they recite verses of Dhamma to him, happy there.
an4.191:2.6: But a monk with psychic power, attained to mastery of awareness, teaches the Dhamma to the assembly of devas.
an4.191:2.7: The thought occurs [to the new deva]:
an4.191:2.8: ‘This is the Dhamma & Vinaya under which I used to live the holy life.’
an4.191:2.9: Slow is the arising of his mindfulness,
an4.191:2.10: but when mindful, he quickly arrives at distinction.
an4.191:2.11: “Suppose a man skilled in the sound of a war drum
an4.191:2.12: were to hear the sound of a war drum while traveling along a highway.
an4.191:2.13: He would have no doubt or perplexity,
an4.191:2.14: ‘Is that the sound of a war drum or not the sound of a war drum?’
an4.191:2.15: He would come to the conclusion, ‘That’s the sound of a war drum for sure.’
an4.191:2.16: In the same way, there is the case where a monk has mastered the Dhamma.…
an4.191:2.19: Passing away when his mindfulness is muddled, he arises in a certain group of devas.…
an4.191:2.21: A monk with psychic power, attained to mastery of awareness, teaches the Dhamma to the assembly of devas.
an4.191:2.22: The thought occurs [to the new deva]:
an4.191:2.23: ‘This is the Dhamma & Vinaya under which I used to live the holy life.’
an4.191:2.24: Slow is the arising of his mindfulness,
an4.191:2.25: but when mindful, he quickly arrives at distinction.
an4.191:2.26: When the teachings have been followed by ear, recited by speech, examined by mind, and well penetrated by view, this is the second reward that can be expected.
an4.191:3.1: “Further, there is the case where a monk has mastered the Dhamma:
an4.191:3.3: In him, these teachings have been followed by ear, recited by speech, examined by mind, and well penetrated by view.
an4.191:3.4: Passing away when his mindfulness is muddled, he arises in a certain group of devas.
an4.191:3.5: It doesn’t happen that they recite verses of Dhamma to him, happy there. Nor does a monk with psychic power, attained to mastery of awareness, teach the Dhamma to the assembly of devas.
an4.191:3.6: But a deva teaches the Dhamma to the assembly of devas.
an4.191:3.7: The thought occurs [to the new deva]:
an4.191:3.8: ‘This is the Dhamma & Vinaya under which I used to live the holy life.’
an4.191:3.9: Slow is the arising of his mindfulness,
an4.191:3.10: but when mindful, he quickly arrives at distinction.
an4.191:3.11: “Suppose a man skilled in the sound of a conch
an4.191:3.12: were to hear the sound of a conch while traveling along a highway.
an4.191:3.13: He would have no doubt or perplexity,
an4.191:3.14: ‘Is that the sound of a conch or not the sound of a conch?’
an4.191:3.15: He would come to the conclusion, ‘That’s the sound of a conch for sure.’
an4.191:3.16: In the same way, there is the case where a monk has mastered the Dhamma.…
an4.191:3.19: Passing away when his mindfulness is muddled, he arises in a certain group of devas.…
an4.191:3.21: A deva teaches the Dhamma to the assembly of devas.
an4.191:3.22: The thought occurs [to the new deva]:
an4.191:3.23: ‘This is the Dhamma & Vinaya under which I used to live the holy life.’
an4.191:3.24: Slow is the arising of his mindfulness,
an4.191:3.25: but when mindful, he quickly arrives at distinction.
an4.191:3.26: When the teachings have been followed by ear, recited by speech, examined by mind, and well penetrated by view, this is the third reward that can be expected.
an4.191:4.1: “Further, there is the case where a monk has mastered the Dhamma:
an4.191:4.3: In him, these teachings have been followed by ear, recited by speech, examined by mind, and well penetrated by view.
an4.191:4.4: Passing away when his mindfulness is muddled, he arises in a certain group of devas.
an4.191:4.5: It doesn’t happen that they recite verses of Dhamma to him, happy there. Nor does a monk with psychic power, attained to mastery of awareness, teach the Dhamma to the assembly of devas. Nor does a deva teach the Dhamma to the assembly of devas.
an4.191:4.6: But [another] spontaneously-arisen being reminds [this] spontaneously-arisen being,
an4.191:4.7: ‘Do you remember, my dear? Do you remember where we practiced the holy life together?’
an4.191:4.10: Slow is the arising of his mindfulness,
an4.191:4.11: but when mindful, he quickly arrives at distinction.
an4.191:4.12: “Suppose that there were two comrades who played together in the mud.
an4.191:4.13: They would happen to meet later at some time, at some place,
an4.191:4.14: and there one companion would say to the other,
an4.191:4.15: ‘Do you remember this, my friend? And do you remember this?’
an4.191:4.18: In the same way, there is the case where a monk has mastered the Dhamma:
an4.191:4.20: In him, these teachings have been followed by ear, recited by speech, examined by mind, and well penetrated by view.
an4.191:4.21: Passing away when his mindfulness is muddled, he arises in a certain group of devas.…
an4.191:4.23: A spontaneously-arisen being reminds [this] spontaneously-arisen being,
an4.191:4.24: ‘Do you remember, my dear? Do you remember where we practiced the holy life together?’
an4.191:4.27: Slow is the arising of his mindfulness,
an4.191:4.28: but when mindful, he quickly arrives at distinction.
an4.191:4.29: When the teachings have been followed by ear, recited by speech, examined by mind, and well penetrated by view, this is the fourth reward that can be expected.
an4.191:4.30: “Monks, when the teachings have been followed by ear, recited by speech, examined by mind, and well penetrated by view, these four rewards can be expected.”
